title: Giants at work
caption: The Very Large Telescope at work under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The enclosures of the Very Large Telescope's Unit Telescopes turn to work under clear skies at ESO's Paranal Observatory, with the Milky Way overhead. On the left, the smaller Auxiliary Telescopes sit in round white domes, and above them hang the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.

ESO Photo Ambassador Gabriel Brammer combined several long exposures to capture the faint Milky Way. That also records the enclosures moving as they follow their targets, each shadowed by a ghostly echo. Time passes across the frame too, from a bright evening sky to a dark, star-speckled view toward the left.

Brammer set up his camera in the same spot twice, once at sunset and once later at night, then joined the two panoramas. Each Unit Telescope stands 25 meters tall, and each carries a name from the language of the local Mapuche people. Antu means the Sun, Kueyen the Moon, Melipal the Southern Cross and Yepun Venus.

understand.summary: This panorama by Gabriel Brammer combines several long-exposure shots taken at sunset and later at night. The source gives no other camera or color details.
understand.eye: No eye could see this at once, because the picture blends different times of evening and records the telescopes' movement as ghostly echoes.

alt: A panorama of large telescope enclosures with ghostly motion echoes under the Milky Way, small white domes at left beneath the Magellanic Clouds, and the sky shading from evening glow to dark night.
